name: Manton Valley

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Merlot, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Merlot, Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Zinfandel is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

soil.rock: Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 5°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
